{\LARGE\bfseries\sffamily\color{AtlasNavy} Low-rank approximation from a finite-bit row stream: one-pass memory\par}\vspace{5pt}
\textbf{Setting ID.} \texttt{MX\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}S\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}stream\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}bits}

Matrix computation

After one pass over the rows of \AtlasInlineMath{A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}}, return a rank-\AtlasInlineMath{k} orthogonal right projection.

\textbf{Status.} Polynomial gap present

\textbf{TASK tags.} formulation: Row streaming lowrank; solution concept: Relative frobenius squared projection; task family: Matrix computation

\textbf{MODEL tags.} spectral structure: Finite encoded matrix; structure: Row stream

\textbf{ORACLE tags.} feedback quality: Exact; interface family: Row stream; operation: Matrix stream update; public information: Hidden objects explicitly declared; public information: Public inputs explicitly declared

\textbf{ALGORITHMS tags.} memory: Finite-bit retained state; randomization: Private randomness allowed; restriction: No past requery; restriction: No additional span restriction explicitly imposed; restriction: One pass

\textbf{OUTPUT tags.} certificate: No additional output certificate required; object: Orthogonal projector or basis

\textbf{METRIC tags.} criterion: Relative squared projection residual

\textbf{GUARANTEE tags.} randomness: Algorithm private seed; time uniformity: Fixed time or accuracy

\textbf{RESOURCE tags.} measure: Memory bits; measure: Passes; measure: Stream rows

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}
After one pass over the rows of \AtlasInlineMath{A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}}, return a rank-\AtlasInlineMath{k} orthogonal right projection.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}
Entries of \AtlasInlineMath{A} lie in the public finite alphabet \AtlasInlineMath{\{0,\pm1,\pm1/\sqrt q\}} with public encoding of integer \AtlasInlineMath{q\ge1}. The row sequence is fixed in advance. Assume \AtlasInlineMath{m,n\ge1}, \AtlasInlineMath{1\le k<\min\{m,n\}}, and \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon>0}.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}
The information \AtlasInlineMath{m,n,k,\varepsilon} and encoding parameter \AtlasInlineMath{q} are public. A call reveals only the next complete row. Consumed rows are unavailable; after the stream, the algorithm cannot query \AtlasInlineMath{Av} or reread the input.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}
After the stream, use only retained state to output \AtlasInlineMath{P=P^{\mathsf T}=P^2\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}} with \AtlasInlineMath{\operatorname{rank}(P)=k}; an orthonormal-basis representation is allowed. Returning \AtlasInlineMath{AP} is unnecessary.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}
Let \AtlasInlineMath{A_k} be any best rank-\AtlasInlineMath{k} Frobenius approximation. Success requires \AtlasInlineMath{\|A(I_n-P)\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2\le(1+\varepsilon)\|A-A_k\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2}; the residual is explicitly squared. When the optimal residual is zero, the row space must be recovered exactly.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}
The native resource is peak simultaneous memory in bits, \AtlasInlineMath{S_{\mathrm{bit}}}. One pass is a fixed protocol requirement and is not added to bit memory. Input encoding, working state, and output-encoding requirements must be retained.

The cost limit holds for every input and private seed. The final output must be decoded from the charged state, without an unregistered external cache.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}
Randomized computable one-pass streaming algorithms are allowed. The retained state is a finite bit string, including random-generator state under the declared memory model. No span or running-time restriction is added beyond one pass and bit memory.

The algorithm is selected using only public inputs. For every admissible input fixed before its private seed is generated, the success event has probability at least \AtlasInlineMath{2/3} over that private randomness.

\textbf{Budget convention.} One pass; peak memory is bounded for every input and random seed.

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{4. Bounds and supporting evidence}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{B1 - Communication lower bound for randomized one-pass row streams, measured in bits of memory}
\textbf{Admission.} Included in the bracket

\textbf{Direction.} lower

\textbf{Witness or lower-bound scope.} The stated restricted randomized class

\AtlasMath{S_{\mathrm{bit}}\ge c\,\frac{nk}{\varepsilon}}
\textbf{Sources.} \href{https://papers.neurips.cc/paper/5407-low-rank-approximation-lower-bounds-in-row-update-streams.pdf}{[1]}

\textbf{Conditions.} For this quantity's worst case over admissible public encodings, use the source construction's \AtlasInlineMath{q=n-r_0}.

\textbf{Dimension conditions.} Assume \AtlasInlineMath{m,n\ge C_0k/\epsilon}. The source hard subclass uses integer \AtlasInlineMath{r_0=\Theta(k/\epsilon)} and \AtlasInlineMath{q=n-r_0}, requiring \AtlasInlineMath{r_0+k} rows; extra rows may be zero padded.

\textbf{Oracle correspondence.} The rows arrive once in a fixed order, with entries exactly encoded over a finite alphabet. Persistent state is finite-bit. Matrix-vector access, rereading, and additional passes are unavailable.

\textbf{Guarantee conversion.} Success probability is at least 2/3 for each fixed admissible encoded input. Randomized state transitions are allowed, and the original sufficient-dimension conditions remain in force.

\textbf{Output rule.} Return an encoding of a right rank-\AtlasInlineMath{k} subspace, with a \AtlasInlineMath{(1+\epsilon)} relative guarantee for squared Frobenius residual. The hard instance uses only the source's finite alphabet.

\textbf{Resource conversion.} The native resource is peak retained bits \AtlasInlineMath{S_{\mathrm{bit}}}. One pass is a fixed protocol and is not added to memory cost. Preserve input encoding, working state, and output encoding. The cap holds for each input and private seed. Final output must decode from charged state, without unrecorded external storage.

\textbf{Simultaneous resource costs.} All coordinates refer to this one witness or necessary constraint.

\textbf{memory bits.}

\AtlasMath{\Omega (nk/eps)}
\textbf{passes.} 1

\textbf{Constants.} Universal constants, with only the parameter dependence permitted by this bound’s region and expression.

\textbf{Source location.} \href{https://papers.neurips.cc/paper/5407-low-rank-approximation-lower-bounds-in-row-update-streams.pdf}{[1]} pdf pages: 2; 3; 4; section: main result and proof; theorem: Theorem 1; construction in §2

ST Theorem 1 gives an \AtlasInlineMath{\Omega(nk/\varepsilon)}-bit memory lower bound for a single-pass randomized row stream with only a right-subspace output. Its construction uses \AtlasInlineMath{[I,R]} and standard-basis rows, with entries of \AtlasInlineMath{R} equal to \AtlasInlineMath{\pm1/\sqrt q}, \AtlasInlineMath{q=n-r_0}, and \AtlasInlineMath{r_0=\Theta(k/\varepsilon)}. This hard subclass has the permitted public encoding.

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy Assign three-bit labels to the five permitted entry values. Duplicate values when q=\allowbreak{}1 cause no difficulty. Append all mn labels in stream order. A current-row buffer,\allowbreak{} counters,\allowbreak{} fixed control and output constructor tag use O(n+log(mn)+1) further bits. Since m,\allowbreak{}n>=\allowbreak{}2,\allowbreak{} the peak and final descriptor sizes are at most 3mn+O(n+log(mn)+1)=\allowbreak{}O(mn). The bound holds deterministically. Public m,\allowbreak{}n,\allowbreak{}k,\allowbreak{}q are available to the interpretation;\allowbreak{} no digits of q are stored.\par\endgroup

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Native item 2}
Native pointer: /proofs/0/argument/1; canonical SHA-256: c5dfd7d095734e688460fe4170c46f4cb322c6a0025f06e534f782b86d509157

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy The output is the retained label array interpreted by a fixed symbolic subspace constructor. It denotes the leading k-dimensional eigenspace of G=\allowbreak{}A\textasciicircum{}T A,\allowbreak{} reconstructing A from its labels and public q. To resolve eigenvalue ties,\allowbreak{} order distinct eigenvalues decreasingly;\allowbreak{} in each eigenspace project e\_\allowbreak{}1,\allowbreak{}...,\allowbreak{}e\_\allowbreak{}n onto that eigenspace and Gram-Schmidt in this order,\allowbreak{} skipping zero remainders and taking positive normalizing roots. Concatenate the resulting orthonormal lists and select their first k vectors. This uniquely defines P=\allowbreak{}sum\_\allowbreak{}\{j<=\allowbreak{}k\}u\_\allowbreak{}j u\_\allowbreak{}j\textasciicircum{}T.\par\endgroup

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Native item 3}
Native pointer: /proofs/0/argument/2; canonical SHA-256: 58cbd5551693fea510ac675f6acc2517ba7a5d49b43e595f008f60e079a82fe5

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy This constructor is the mathematical interpretation of the permitted symbolic output,\allowbreak{} not a numerical eigensolver executed in uncharged working space. Every input-dependent datum in that representation remains in the charged label array. For each integer q all entries are algebraic,\allowbreak{} and the canonical spectral rule has a computable exact interpretation. No input rereading,\allowbreak{} external cache,\allowbreak{} evaluated coordinates or exact-real registers are used by the streaming computation. A model requiring evaluated coordinate output would need a different proof;\allowbreak{} the frozen view expressly permits symbolic subspace descriptions.\par\endgroup

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Native item 4}
Native pointer: /proofs/0/argument/3; canonical SHA-256: 88bcc37f5155766afd78850fa684802cd37a985463aeec3349db271b7aa6d584

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy Let lambda\_\allowbreak{}1>=\allowbreak{}...>=\allowbreak{}lambda\_\allowbreak{}n>=\allowbreak{}0 be the eigenvalues of G. For any rank-k orthogonal Q,\allowbreak{} its diagonal weights w\_\allowbreak{}j in this eigenbasis lie in [0,\allowbreak{}1] and sum to k. Moving weight to larger eigenvalues gives tr(GQ)=\allowbreak{}sum lambda\_\allowbreak{}j w\_\allowbreak{}j <=\allowbreak{} sum\_\allowbreak{}\{j<=\allowbreak{}k\}lambda\_\allowbreak{}j. The constructed P attains equality,\allowbreak{} hence ||A(I-P)||\_\allowbreak{}F\textasciicircum{}2=\allowbreak{}sum\_\allowbreak{}\{j>k\}lambda\_\allowbreak{}j.\par\endgroup

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Native item 5}
Native pointer: /proofs/0/argument/4; canonical SHA-256: 04bc2cd6465062e84446f20052d8915bc016ce4b9656723760a6e71fc4520af1

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy For any rank-at-most-k matrix B,\allowbreak{} extend its row space to a k-dimensional subspace with projector Q. Orthogonality gives ||A-B||\_\allowbreak{}F\textasciicircum{}2=\allowbreak{}||A(I-Q)||\_\allowbreak{}F\textasciicircum{}2+||AQ-B||\_\allowbreak{}F\textasciicircum{}2 >=\allowbreak{} sum\_\allowbreak{}\{j>k\}lambda\_\allowbreak{}j. B=\allowbreak{}AP attains equality. Thus the output achieves exactly ||A-A\_\allowbreak{}k||\_\allowbreak{}F\textasciicircum{}2,\allowbreak{} meeting g1 for every epsilon>0 with probability one. If rank(A)<k,\allowbreak{} canonical nullspace vectors complete the subspace to rank exactly k,\allowbreak{} with zero residual.\par\endgroup

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy Retain the exact accepted native b1 lower and b2 upper,\allowbreak{} including their view main/\allowbreak{}g1/\allowbreak{}q1/\allowbreak{}resource and all original R guards. The minimax quantity is worst-case over the admissible public encodings q,\allowbreak{} not an individually fixed-q complexity. The b1 source construction supplies S\_\allowbreak{}bits\textasciicircum{}star >=\allowbreak{} c n k/\allowbreak{}epsilon on R. The fully charged deterministic construction p\_\allowbreak{}store supplies S\_\allowbreak{}bits\textasciicircum{}star <=\allowbreak{} 3mn+O(n+log(mn)+1) <=\allowbreak{} C mn with universal C on D,\allowbreak{} uniformly in the public q,\allowbreak{} using the existing symbolic-output contract and no additional input access. Since k<min(m,\allowbreak{}n),\allowbreak{} both m,\allowbreak{}n>=\allowbreak{}2 and the stated overhead is absorbed uniformly. On S=\allowbreak{}R intersect\{m<=\allowbreak{}2 C\_\allowbreak{}0 k/\allowbreak{}epsilon\},\allowbreak{} the upper is at most 2 C C\_\allowbreak{}0 n k/\allowbreak{}epsilon. Thus c n k/\allowbreak{}epsilon <=\allowbreak{} S\_\allowbreak{}bits\textasciicircum{}star <=\allowbreak{} 2 C C\_\allowbreak{}0 n k/\allowbreak{}epsilon:\allowbreak{} Theta(nk/\allowbreak{}epsilon),\allowbreak{} with only universal source constants C\_\allowbreak{}0,\allowbreak{}epsilon\_\allowbreak{}0 fixed,\allowbreak{} never hiding m,\allowbreak{}n,\allowbreak{}k,\allowbreak{}epsilon or q. This also equals Theta(mn) on S since C\_\allowbreak{}0 k/\allowbreak{}epsilon<=\allowbreak{}m<=\allowbreak{}2 C\_\allowbreak{}0 k/\allowbreak{}epsilon. The upper succeeds deterministically and has the native pathwise memory cap,\allowbreak{} hence preserves per-input success >=\allowbreak{}2/\allowbreak{}3. Its finite-label charged output handles zero optimal residual and rank deficiency by the existing canonical exact spectral interpretation;\allowbreak{} we do not replace it with a numerical coordinate-output algorithm or free external eigensolver. No new output,\allowbreak{} finite precision,\allowbreak{} RAM-word,\allowbreak{} oracle/\allowbreak{}pass or q-pointwise assumption is introduced. S is nonempty as a parameter region:\allowbreak{} set k=\allowbreak{}1,\allowbreak{} choose epsilon=\allowbreak{}min(epsilon\_\allowbreak{}0/\allowbreak{}2,\allowbreak{}C\_\allowbreak{}0/\allowbreak{}4,\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}4)>0,\allowbreak{} and m=\allowbreak{}n=\allowbreak{}ceil(C\_\allowbreak{}0/\allowbreak{}epsilon);\allowbreak{} C\_\allowbreak{}0/\allowbreak{}epsilon>=\allowbreak{}4 ensures m<=\allowbreak{}2 C\_\allowbreak{}0/\allowbreak{}epsilon and k<min(m,\allowbreak{}n). The source lower still ranges over its own legal encoding subclass,\allowbreak{} not necessarily q=\allowbreak{}1. The equality m=\allowbreak{}2 C\_\allowbreak{}0 k/\allowbreak{}epsilon is included whenever integral;\allowbreak{} epsilon=\allowbreak{}epsilon\_\allowbreak{}0 is not. Outside S the old c1 remains polynomial\_\allowbreak{}gap on R,\allowbreak{} and D minus R remains unassessed. This is publication of a closure already explicitly stated in the baseline joint annotation,\allowbreak{} not a new source theorem,\allowbreak{} a strict extension beyond R,\allowbreak{} or a full-domain minimax solution.\par\endgroup
